attributes.residual: STACK_LAYOUT, CAPPED, but the residual is now LOCATED TO A SINGLE WEB, which is the deliverable and a strict advance on the prior record's two guesses. THE MECHANISM: our extra callee-saved GPR r25 holds exactly one value -- the loop-top address `r31 + r26` (sItemRuntime base plus the byte index i*4). Ours defines it at `bc: add r25,r31,r26`, consumes it at `c0: lwz r0,29216(r25)` for the `runtime->wobjTarget[i] == target` compare, and then KEEPS IT ALIVE ACROSS THE ErrorPrintf CALL at 0x120 for a single further use at `13c: stfs f31,0(r25)`. The target lets the same value die at the compare (`b8: add r3,r31,r26`, a volatile register) and rematerialises the store as the indexed form `13c: stfsx f31,r31,r26`. That is the whole gap: the surviving 2-token multiset (target-only +1 stfsx, ours-only -1 stfs) IS this web's store, and every frame and slot delta follows from it -- six callee-saved GPRs (r25-r31) against the target's five (r26-r31), pushing the saved block down 4 bytes (`lmw r25,52(r1)` vs `lmw r26,48(r1)`) and rounding the frame to 96 against 88. ONE error, not four, and not two suspects. NOTE the web buys us nothing: `stfsx f31,r31,r26` and `stfs f31,0(r25)` are one instruction each, so r25 is a pure allocator artefact, not a code-size win. HANDOFF SUSPECTS ELIMINATED: the prior record nominated 'the early home `mr r28,r4` of `type` and the early `clrlwi r3,r4,24`'. Neither is the cause. Axis C moved the narrowing's assignment order and the object came back BYTE-IDENTICAL, and both `mr r28,r4` and the `clrlwi` sit in the entry block whose multiset NETS TO ZERO (target and ours differ only in the order of `mr`/`lis`/`cmplwi`/`addi`/`clrlwi`); the entry region is pure intra-block scheduling and is NOT what allocates r25. DO NOT RE-PROBE: the direct-global respelling of any `runtime->` site (axis B, costs a second symbol root), the deletion of `trigger_type` (v1 axis A2), the deletion of the `wtarget` alias (v1 axis A3), and declaration/initializer reordering (axis C, null). ALSO CONFIRMED RETIRED: this is not WebFrank-eligible -- the STRUCTURAL rows include the frame arithmetic itself (`addi r1,r1,88` vs `addi r1,r1,96`, `lmw r26,48(r1)` vs `lmw r25,52(r1)`), and no recolor or permutation rule can change a frame size or a save set. THE ONE OPEN QUESTION for the next pass is narrow and now well posed: find a source form that makes MWCC let the loop-top address temp DIE at the compare, without introducing a second address root -- i.e. a lever over an implicit compiler-formed address temp's live range across a call. The corpus currently names no such lever; if one is found it is a new law, and closing this single web is predicted to flip the function exact, since it is the sole source of both the 2-token multiset and the entire frame/save-set delta.
